descriptions: The name of the course, as printed.
The course number or code, such as CHEM 1A or MATH 2210.
A general description of what the course covers.
The degree, program or department the course belongs to.
The level of the course: introductory, upper division, graduate.
The kind of class: lecture, lab, seminar, discussion section.
The name of the person teaching the course.
When and where the instructor is available to students, such as "Wednesdays 2-4pm in room 312".
An email address, phone number or office location.
How many credits or units the course is worth.
How many students may enrol, or how many seats remain.
The section number or section identifier of a class.
What a student must have to be admitted to the course.
Who may or may not take the course: majors, standing, consent.
Whether the student is registered, admitted or confirmed.
Courses or knowledge required before taking this course.
The topics, schedule of topics or material covered in class.
What a student will be able to do after the course.
How the course is taught: in person, online, hybrid.
Required textbooks, software, equipment or supplies for the course.
Readings assigned for particular weeks or classes.
Homework, papers, projects or other graded work.
The date something is due or an exam is scheduled.
How the grade is calculated, including weights, percentages and cut-offs.
Letter grades, grade scales or grade point values.
How students are evaluated: exams, quizzes, participation.
How students evaluate the course or instructor, such as an end-of-term survey.
The clock time a class meets.
The days of the week a class meets.
The room or building where a class meets.
Whether attendance is required or the course is remote.
A calendar of sessions, topics or events in the course.
When exams, midterms or the final exam take place, including dates and durations.
The start and end dates of the term or session.
The academic term or semester, such as Fall 2024.
The last day to drop or add the course.
The rules about attending class and the consequences of absence, such as excused absences or a participation requirement.
The rules about cheating, plagiarism and collaboration.
Other course rules: late work, electronics, conduct.
Accommodations for a disability and the office that arranges them, such as extended time on exams.
Other administrative notes about the course.
Text that is not any academic field: navigation, ads, page furniture.
